stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def f(g):
    g=[r[:] for r in g]
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(x for row in g for x in row)
    bg=max(cnt,key=lambda c:cnt[c])
    obj=[c for c,_ in cnt.items() if c!=bg][0]
    cells=[(r,c) for r in range(len(g)) for c in range(len(g[0])) if g[r][c]==obj]
    r0=min(r for r,c in cells); r1=max(r for r,c in cells)
    c1=max(c for r,c in cells)
    for r in range(r0,r1+1):
        for c in range(c1+1,len(g[0])):
            if g[r][c]==bg: g[r][c]=1
    return g

Demo 6: bg=2, obj=8. Row2 cols10-14 changed 2->1; row12 col14 2->1. In demo6, the "background" is 2 and object 8. Changed cells are bg-colored (2) → 1. Where? Row 2: input '888222228822222' — shape at cols 0-2 (8s), then 2s cols3-7, 8 at 8-9, 2s rest. Hmm row 2 has 8s at 0-2 and 8-9. Changed 2→1 at cols 10-14.

Row 12: '888888222228882': 8s cols0-5, 2s 6-10, 8s 11-13, 2 at 14 → changed to 1.

So in both demos, a run of bg color immediately following the last object cell in a row gets recolored to 1. Check: pair5 rows 18-23: each row ends with 8s (cols8-10 = 4s) after the last 2 (col 7). So yes: trailing background run after the last object cell in the row → 1. Pair5 row 10 is all 2s (no bg trailing... it's fully object, no change). Rows 5-9 have internal structure but trailing after last 2: row 7 last 2 at col10, nothing after. Row 8 last 2 at col10. So consistent: after the final non-bg cell, any remaining cells in that row become 1.

But wait — would that apply to EVERY row containing an object? In pair5, rows 5-9 contain objects too, yet unchanged. E.g., row5 '44222222222' no trailing bg. Row 7 '44222242222' ends in 2. Row 8 '44224422222' ends in 2. So all rows with object end with the object or... actually they end with obj or obj adjacent to edge. Only the bottom block had trailing bg. In pair6, row 2 ends with 2→1; other rows like row 3 '222822882222222' ends in 2! And didn't change. Hmm.

Row 3: '222822882222222': 8s at 3, 5-6, then 2s to col14. Trailing bg after last 8 (col6) is cols 7-14 — not changed. But row 2 changed cols 10-14, and row 12 changed col 14.

Difference: row 2 is the topmost row of the shape? Shape occupies rows 2-6 roughly. Row 2 is first row. Row 12 is... rows 12-17 second shape block. Not first row of its block. Hmm.

Alternative: maybe only the rightmost column strip per shape gets filled? Like fill between rightmost object cell and grid right edge for rows within the shape's vertical extent. Pair6 shape vertical extent rows 2-24? That would recolor many rows. Only rows 2 and 12 changed.

Hmm, think about structure differently. Maybe each shape (multi-row blob) should be a full rectangle, and missing columns get filled with 1 — but colored 1 as "filled gap"? In pair5 bottom shape spans cols 0-8; filling cols 8-10 across rows 18-23 completes to width 11? The top shape spans cols 2-10 already. Filling gaps makes shapes rectangular. In pair6, shape at top-left spans cols 0-2 (rows 2-6), plus stray 8s at (2,8),(2,9)? Actually row 2 has 8s at 0-2 and 8-9. These might be separate components.

Different idea: 1 marks the region where the shape would continue — i.e., each component gets extended to the grid's right edge in the rows where it touches the top/bottom of the component's bounding box? For pair6 top shape: bbox rows 2-6, cols 0-2 (with protrusions). Extending to right edge in rows 2-6 would recolor many rows. No.

Look again: pair6 changes happen at row 2 (top of top group) and row 12 (top of middle group). Groups: rows2-6 (shape A), rows 12-17 (shape B), rows 19-24 (shape C). Group A top row: cols0-2 are 8s, followed by 2s until col 8 which has 8s at 8,9? Row 2: 888 22222 88 22222. Changes at cols 10-14 = after the last 8 (col 9). Group B top row 12: 888888 22222 888 2; change at col14, after last 8 (col13). Group C top row 19: 888 222222 888888888 — full to edge, no change. 

Interesting: in each group, the top row's rightmost segment... In group A top row, there's an 8-protrusion at cols 8-9 beyond the main block (cols 0-2). Then after cols 8-9, the row continues with 2s. Change fills those trailing 2s. Group B top row: main 8s 0-5, gap 6-10, 8s 11-13, then single 2 at 14 → changed. So pattern: if the topmost row of a connected component (of non-bg) doesn't reach the right edge, extend/bg after last obj → 1. But why only top row? Because in rows 3+, the shape extends leftward... hmm.
